params.baseInstructions: Complete the supplied mathematical task using only its explicit inputs and tools. Submit the requested JSON artifact through submit_artifact. Tool feedback is real task feedback; do not invent a successful check. This is a Yui workflow stage. Read the relevant declared Yui rules, preserve the supplied proof route and exact allowed assumptions, and distinguish mathematical review from structural checks.

dynamicTools.name: search_mathlib
dynamicTools.description: 在固定 mathlib 的 Lean 源码中搜索正则表达式，返回至多 100 行。

dynamicTools.name: read_mathlib
dynamicTools.description: 读取固定 mathlib 中一个 Mathlib/...lean 文件的指定行。

dynamicTools.name: read_task_input
dynamicTools.description: Read an explicitly frozen task document by ID; no other local files are accessible.

dynamicTools.name: read_yui
dynamicTools.description: Read declared Yui rules/templates; no tests, historical runs or personal files.

dynamicTools.name: check_artifact
dynamicTools.description: Check a JSON artifact against the explicit stage contract; this is not automatic mathematical certification.

dynamicTools.name: submit_artifact
dynamicTools.description: Submit a JSON artifact after its stage checks.

dynamicTools.name: report_obstacle
dynamicTools.description: Stop this stage honestly on a substantive or suspected proof gap, unavailable source, or input conflict. JSON fields: status, location, explanation, basis, partial_progress. Status must be SUBSTANTIVE_GAP, SUSPECTED_GAP, SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE or INPUT_CONFLICT. Difficulty alone is not a mathematical error.

dynamicTools.name: probe_library
dynamicTools.description: Query a proved Mathlib theorem and its exact signature/axioms in the offline sandbox. Returns located evidence for an M source; the mathematical statement and applicability still require review.

input.text:
Make a bounded correction to the supplied unaccepted Lie NL0, using actual global-review findings as diagnostic candidate feedback. Read every task input and relevant Yui rules. The reviewer found that characteristic-zero e_i were subsequently used as reduced K-basis vectors without explicitly defining that new basis and action correspondence from a e_i. Repair the notation/representation identity, all needed declarations and the precise reduction/matrix-unit reasoning; do not silently equate complex and characteristic-p vectors or assume a is a unit. Preserve the original target/hypotheses and existing proof route and unchanged mathematics. Use {base_input:"prior-candidate.json",patches:[...]} for exact local edits, including related local facts/inventories. Every patch submission starts from that immutable base; no full proof rewrite is required. If any further ordinary omission is noticed, supply it or its actual source rather than assuming it under a calculation-policy sentence. A schema check is not Audit A. Submit the corrected complete artifact for a new independent audit; do not issue your own acceptance verdict.

Canonical submission has exactly {"spec": <NL0 v2 specification>, "graph": <NL0 v2 graph>}. For a local revision, you may instead submit {"base_input":"<frozen task document ID>", "patches":[{"op":"replace","path":"/graph/...","value":...}]}. That declared task document must itself contain {spec,graph}; supported JSON edit operations are add/remove/replace/test with absolute JSON pointers inside spec or graph. Edits always start from that immutable base, not the last rejected edit. Array append uses /-. The expanded result undergoes every ordinary metadata/source/structure gate and later Audit A. This saves retyping unchanged content; it does not change mathematical authority. The controller binds spec.inputs to all frozen task documents, pins to the verified runtime, and graph.spec_sha256 to the resulting spec. Supply these fields as placeholders if needed. All mathematical fields remain your responsibility. probe_library returns checked M-source evidence inside this stage case directory. The controller binds M signature, source hashes, declaration kind, commit and evidence from the actual successful probe matching its ID, declaration and dotted module. These metadata fields may be omitted; never transcribe or fabricate them. It does not change source.statement, hypotheses, binders or proof text; all still need complete mathematical content. Redundant aliases may also be omitted: H graph statement copies its own spec.hypotheses statement, P statement copies spec.conclusion, and E/M source.statement copies its primary proposition.statement. Existing conflicting texts are rejected, never silently rewritten. Actual source signatures/source_statement remain separate fidelity obligations. A successful check_artifact is structural validation, not Audit A acceptance.
Frozen structural contract: spec.format_version=2; graph.format_version=2; spec.case_id=graph.case_id="lie-module-irreducibility". The controller-bound pins are {"lean_version": "4.32.2", "mathlib_commit": "905b95818eb32af7874a58b427f50c1711a5e96c", "mathlib_root": "/Users/syyui/formalization-tools/lean-mathlib-v4.32.2/mathlib"}. These are provided configuration facts, not guessed mathematical premises. Spec.inputs, spec.pins and graph.spec_sha256 are rebound deterministically, so their placeholder values are not an input conflict. All other required schema fields must be supplied normally.
Exact permitted machine rule names for spec.logic.rules and inference.rules: ["case_elimination", "contradiction_classical", "direct", "exists_elimination", "forall_introduction", "implication_introduction", "modus_ponens", "natural_induction", "negation_introduction"]. Use these identifiers; put mathematical derivations in argument text, not invented rule enum values. Parameters are a list of {symbol,type}; logic is an object {classical,rules,calculations,primitives}. Inferences use R001-style IDs; argument paragraphs use S001-style IDs; propositions use H001/E001/M001/N001 or P. An unknown field/rule is a format repair, not a mathematical gap. Read references/nl0-format.md for every remaining field.
Yui entry: read_yui(path="SKILL.md", start=1, end=200). Available frozen rule paths (relative to rigorous-proof): SKILL.md, references/audit-a.md, references/external-theorems.md, references/isolation.md, references/lean-handoff.md, references/logical-rules.md, references/measurement.md, references/nl0-authoring.md, references/nl0-format.md, references/nl0-stage.md, references/self-containment.md, templates/audit-a.md, templates/authoring.md, templates/submission-example.md, translation/references/architecture.md, translation/references/audit-b.md, translation/references/design-notes.md, translation/references/experiments.md, translation/references/integrated-workflow.md, translation/references/obstacle-routing.md, translation/references/shared-lemmas.md, translation/references/source-refactoring.md, translation/references/stage.md, translation/references/translation-rules.md, translation/references/workflow.md, translation/templates/audit-b.md, translation/templates/source-refactoring.md. Every read supports at most 250 lines. Start with the entry and follow its relevant links; do not guess filenames.
Frozen task document IDs: completed-proof.json, execution-qualification.txt, global-findings.json, prior-candidate.json, problem.md, source-context.md. Use read_task_input to read them.
